subject: OrbitX private VPC deployment — playbook & handoff review
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@orbitx.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: cloudops@orbitx.com
Date: 2027-07-11T12:22:00-04:00
Subject: OrbitX private VPC deployment — initial review request

Sean —

Thanks again for the call this morning. OrbitX is preparing a private deployment of Redwood (control plane in our AWS account, data plane on dedicated on-prem GPUs). We attached a short requirements doc (orbitx_requirements_v1.docx). High-level asks:

- Control plane must be reachable from our management subnet only (no public endpoints).
- Data plane will sit behind our private VLAN; egress must be via a controlled NAT / proxy we operate.
- We need a clear runbook for upgrades that includes a canary path and fallback.
- Audit logs and request traces for 90 days retained in our S3.

Can you send a short playbook and topology sketch we can review before a joint architecture session? We're aiming to start validation next week (week of 7/19).

Thanks — Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Ops, OrbitX

(attachment: orbitx_requirements_v1.docx)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@orbitx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-11T14:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: OrbitX private VPC deployment — initial review request

Liam —

Appreciate the detailed requirements. Attaching our deploy playbook (redwood-vpc-deploy-playbook-v1.pdf) and a short annotated topology. Quick summary of the recommended design:

- Control plane: customer-managed VPC with private subnets hosting the control-plane control plane agents (HTTPS over mutual TLS). We recommend a small control-plane bastion subnet for operator access and a private ALB with security groups limited to your management CIDR.
- Data plane: on-prem nodes in your VLAN that initiate outbound, authenticated TLS connections to control-plane agents (pull model). This keeps ingress into your datacenter minimal.
- Egress: we support either a customer proxy (recommended) or our managed egress gateway (falls under Dedicated billing). For OrbitX you said you want full control — we'll configure our services to use your proxy with mTLS and specific SNI routing.
- Upgrades: canary by pool (10% nodes) + automatic rollback if latency/error regressions exceed thresholds. Runbook section 4 has the step-by-step.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick architecture review call (30m) with your cloudops and our infra (Marissa/Diego) — can you do 7/13 10:00–11:00 PT?
2) We’ll provide a draft mutual action plan and a test harness for KV/cache warmup.

Notes / open items for the call: how strictly do you require inbound connectivity for health checks (we can operate entirely over TLS outbound but some customers prefer an internal health relay)? Also need S3 write pattern (direct vs via proxy).

Attaching: redwood-vpc-deploy-playbook-v1.pdf (topology diagram included).

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-vpc-deploy-playbook-v1.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-11T16:30:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: OrbitX private VPC deployment — initial review request

Sean / Diego —

Quick internal notes after reading Liam's requirements and the playbook draft (see below). Forwarding with inline comments.

> From Sean: Control plane: customer-managed VPC with private subnets...
> Comment (Marissa): Agree with private ALB and management CIDR restriction. We should add explicit IAM role scoping for the control-plane agents (least privilege).

> From Sean: Data plane: on-prem nodes in your VLAN that initiate outbound, authenticated TLS connections to control-plane agents (pull model).
> Comment (Diego): Need to confirm whether OrbitX load balancer supports client cert rotation; if not, we fall back to short-lived token auth. Also want to validate that on-prem KV cache is pre-warmed during handoff (we should include a cache-warm script).

Open checklist items for handoff call:
- Egress pattern: confirm if OrbitX will run a proxy that allows SNI inspection. If not, propose an egress firewall rule set we can recommend.
- Audit logs: 90 days retention in OrbitX S3 — confirm bucket lifecycle policies and encryption (KMS key ARN).
- Upgrade window: propose nightly canary during low-traffic window as default; allow scheduled maintenance override.

I've annotated the PDF with suggested runbook changes (attachment: redwood-vpc-deploy-playbook-v1-annotated.pdf). I'll take lead on the canary/rollback section during the call. Diego, can you pull the deployment scripts into a validation branch before 7/18?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-vpc-deploy-playbook-v1-annotated.pdf)

Quoted-For-Context: Liam's original mail (orbitx_requirements_v1.docx attached).

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@orbitx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-12T09:15:00-04:00
Subject: OrbitX private VPC deployment — agreed next steps & MAP

Liam —

Thanks for the fast turn. Following our internal review we've updated the playbook and sketched a short mutual action plan (MAP). High-level decisions:

- Control plane will live in OrbitX-managed AWS VPC (private subnets behind a private ALB). Access: management CIDR + operator bastion.
- Data plane will be on-prem clusters in OrbitX VLANs and will initiate outbound connections to the control plane (TLS mTLS preferred; fallback to short-lived tokens).
- Egress must traverse OrbitX proxy/NAT. Redwood will be configured to accept telemetry and artifact uploads via that proxy only.
- Retention: Audit logs shipped to OrbitX S3, 90 days lifecycle; Redwood will provide a delivery validation job and SHA-256 manifest for each upload.

Immediate next steps (action owners and ETA):
1) OrbitX: share proxy SNI whitelist + KMS key ARN (Liam) — due 2027-07-14.
2) Redwood: create validation branch with the cache-warm and canary scripts (Diego) — due 2027-07-18.
3) Redwood: formal MAP in XLS and shared Drive folder with timeline and rollback criteria (Sean/Marissa) — draft by 2027-07-13.
4) Joint architecture call (30m) — target 2027-07-13 10:00 PT (please confirm).

Links: Drive playbook (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/OrbitX/VPC-playbook-v1), JIRA RED-4821 for deployment tasks, HubSpot record HS-ORBITX-119.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-orbitx.xlsx (draft).

If that aligns, we'll lock the call and start the validation branch.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
